template.name: germany_undergrad_university_selection
template.description: Interview to plan an undergraduate university choice in Germany by mapping options, clarifying decision criteria, confirming admissions feasibility, and defining an application plan.

sections.label: Academic Profile and Goals
sections.description: Capture the student's intended field(s) of study, academic strengths/interests, language proficiency, and long-term goals to anchor fit and program selection.

sections.label: Candidate Universities and Programs
sections.description: Record each specific university and undergraduate program being considered with degree title, language of instruction, location, intake/start date, and the student's reason for interest (do not include requirements here).

sections.label: Admissions Requirements and Eligibility
sections.description: List concrete entry requirements for target programs (grades, subject prerequisites, Uni‑Assist, APS, language/tests, documents, deadlines) and note the student’s current status and any gaps to close.

sections.label: Decision Criteria and Priority Weights
sections.description: Document the factors the student will use to choose (e.g., curriculum fit, teaching language, reputation, location, internships, class size) and how important each is; use this for priorities, while concrete costs or funding go to Financial Plan.

sections.label: Financial Plan and Budget
sections.description: Detail tuition/semester contributions, expected living costs by city, scholarships or funding sources, part-time work assumptions, and the student’s budget limits or constraints.

sections.label: Information Gaps and Research Tasks
sections.description: Capture unanswered questions and assign research actions (what to find, who will do it, and by when), including contacts, campus visits, info sessions, or document verifications.

sections.label: Stakeholders and Decision Process
sections.description: Note who is involved in advising or deciding, who funds the studies, the intended decision timeline and checkpoints, and how tie-breaks will be resolved.

sections.label: Application Timeline and Next Steps
sections.description: Lay out key deadlines (Uni‑Assist, university applications, language tests, visas), target submission dates, and the immediate next actions with owners and due dates.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Goals
phases.goal: Build rapport, clarify the student’s aims for studying in Germany, and agree on success criteria for this conversation.

phases.label: Map Options and Requirements
phases.goal: Elicit concrete programs/universities in scope, capture their admissions requirements, and begin defining the student’s decision criteria.

phases.label: Compare and Narrow
phases.goal: Evaluate options against priorities and budget to form a prioritized shortlist and surface remaining unknowns.

phases.label: Plan and Wrap
phases.goal: Convert the shortlist into an action plan with deadlines and owners, and confirm the decision process and checkpoints.

issues.description: Section admissions_requirements_and_eligibility asks to capture “deadlines,” which overlaps with application_timeline_and_next_steps (“key deadlines … target submission dates”). This breaks MECE and will cause mis-bucketing of date info.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove “deadlines” from admissions_requirements_and_eligibility and add an explicit note: do not capture dates/windows here; all dates and application windows go in application_timeline_and_next_steps. Keep admissions focused on requirement types and current eligibility status/gaps.

issues.description: decision_criteria_and_priority_weights is marked repeated=true, which is ambiguous (is each entry a criterion, or a per-program criterion set?). The label implies a single global weighting framework.
issues.suggested_fix: Set repeated=false and capture a list of criteria with relative weights within one entry; or, if keeping repeated=true, state explicitly that each entry is one global criterion (not per program) and include a numeric weight/scale field.

issues.description: Financial considerations only appear in the Evaluate and Narrow phase. Budget constraints often shape option surfacing; leaving them late can cause rework.
issues.suggested_fix: Lightly introduce financial_plan_and_budget in the Map Options and Requirements phase to record basic budget constraints/cost sensitivity, while keeping detailed costing for the Evaluate phase.

critique.rationale: Solid structure and pacing with clear, concrete sections that fit the user’s goal of identifying options and decision factors for studying in Germany. However, the admissions vs. timeline split is not clean: both ask for deadlines, which will confuse data capture. Minor polish on how criteria are modeled and when to surface budget would make this template crisper.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Eliminate the deadlines overlap by moving all date/window content to application_timeline_and_next_steps and explicitly excluding dates from admissions_requirements_and_eligibility.

template.name: germany_undergrad_university_selection
template.description: Interview to plan an undergraduate university choice in Germany by mapping options, clarifying decision criteria, confirming admissions feasibility (without dates), and defining an application plan.

sections.label: Academic Profile and Goals
sections.description: Capture the student's intended field(s) of study, academic record/strengths, language proficiency (German/English with test status), and long-term goals to anchor fit and program selection.

sections.label: Candidate Universities and Programs
sections.description: Record each specific university and bachelor program under consideration with degree title, language of instruction, location, intake/start term, and the student’s reason for interest; do not include admissions requirements or any dates here.

sections.label: Admissions Requirements and Eligibility
sections.description: List concrete entry requirement types for target programs (grades, subject prerequisites, Studienkolleg/APS, Uni-Assist, language/tests, documents, selection procedures) and note the student’s current status and any gaps to close; do not capture any deadlines or dates here—put all dates/windows in Application Timeline.

sections.label: Decision Criteria and Priority Weights
sections.description: Define a single global set of decision criteria (e.g., curriculum fit, teaching language, reputation, location, internships, class size, international support) with relative weights or ranking; keep objective costs in Financial Plan and per-program facts in Candidate Universities.

sections.label: Financial Plan and Budget
sections.description: Detail tuition/semester contributions, estimated living costs by city, expected funding or scholarships, part-time work assumptions, and the student’s budget caps or constraints.

sections.label: Information Gaps and Research Tasks
sections.description: Capture unanswered questions and assign internal research actions (what to find, who will do it, and target date), including contacts, campus visits, info sessions, or document verifications; reserve formal application/test/visa deadlines for Application Timeline.

sections.label: Stakeholders and Decision Process
sections.description: Note who is involved in advising or deciding, who funds the studies, the intended decision cadence and checkpoints, and how tie-breaks will be resolved.

sections.label: Application Timeline and Next Steps
sections.description: Lay out key application and test deadlines, application windows, visa milestones, and target submission dates, and list the immediate next actions with owners and due dates.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Goals
phases.goal: Build rapport, clarify the student’s aims for studying in Germany, and agree on success criteria for this conversation.

phases.label: Map Options and Requirements
phases.goal: Elicit concrete programs/universities in scope, capture their admissions requirement types and current eligibility, establish initial budget constraints, and begin defining the global decision criteria.

phases.label: Compare and Narrow
phases.goal: Evaluate options against priorities and budget to form a prioritized shortlist and surface remaining unknowns.

phases.label: Plan and Wrap
phases.goal: Convert the shortlist into an action plan with deadlines and owners, and confirm the decision process and checkpoints.

issues.description: Task ownership and due-dates are split across two sections: `information_gaps_and_research_tasks` (assigns research actions with target dates) and `application_timeline_and_next_steps` (lists immediate next actions with owners and due dates). This overlap will cause mis-bucketing of action items (e.g., "email admissions by Friday").
issues.suggested_fix: Confine `application_timeline_and_next_steps` to external deadlines/milestones only (application/test windows, visa milestones) and remove action lists from it; centralize all action items with owners/dates in `information_gaps_and_research_tasks` (or create a distinct `action_items_and_owners` section). Update both descriptions accordingly.

issues.description: `candidate_universities_and_programs` asks for "intake/start term" while also instructing "do not include any dates here," which is contradictory.
issues.suggested_fix: Either remove "intake/start term" from this section, or clarify to capture only the standard intake semester label (Winter/Summer) without specific dates; keep all concrete windows/deadlines in `application_timeline_and_next_steps`.

issues.description: `financial_plan_and_budget` is marked `repeated=true`, which suggests multiple separate budget entries and may fragment a single coherent budget picture.
issues.suggested_fix: Set `repeated=false` and note that per-city/per-option cost breakdowns should be captured within the single budget entry. If you truly want per-option budgets, state that explicitly (e.g., "one entry per city/program scenario").

missing_aspects: EU vs non‑EU citizenship/residency and country of secondary schooling (drives HZB/Anabin, APS, visa relevance) are not explicitly captured in `academic_profile_and_goals` but are material for Germany-specific feasibility and costs.
critique.rationale: Overall structure, pacing, and naming are strong and well-aligned with choosing a German undergraduate program. However, the action-item overlap between Information Gaps and Application Timeline will likely confuse filing and retrieval, and there is a small contradiction about dates in the options section. Addressing these will make the template cleaner and easier to use.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Eliminate the action-item overlap by restricting `application_timeline_and_next_steps` to external deadlines/milestones and centralizing all owned action items in a single section.

template.name: germany_undergrad_university_selection
template.description: Interview to plan an undergraduate university choice in Germany by mapping options, clarifying decision criteria, checking admissions feasibility, and organizing external deadlines and owned actions for applications.

sections.label: Academic Profile and Goals
sections.description: Capture the student's intended field(s), academic record/strengths, language proficiency (German/English with test status), citizenship/residency (EU vs non‑EU) and country/curriculum of secondary schooling (HZB/Anabin or APS/visa relevance), and long‑term goals to anchor fit and feasibility.

sections.label: Candidate Universities and Programs
sections.description: Record each specific university and bachelor program under consideration with degree title, language of instruction, location, and intake semester label (Winter/Summer only—no specific dates), plus the student’s reason for interest; do not include admissions requirements here.

sections.label: Admissions Requirements and Eligibility
sections.description: List concrete entry requirement types for target programs (grades/NC, subject prerequisites, Studienkolleg, APS, Uni‑Assist, language/tests, documents, selection procedures) and note the student’s current status and any gaps to close; do not capture any deadlines or dates here—put all dates/windows in External Deadlines and Milestones.

sections.label: Decision Criteria and Priority Weights
sections.description: Define a single global set of decision criteria (e.g., curriculum fit, teaching language, reputation, location, internships, class size, international support) with relative weights or ranking; keep objective costs in Financial Plan and per‑program facts in Candidate Universities.

sections.label: Financial Plan and Budget
sections.description: Provide a consolidated budget view (tuition/semester contributions, estimated living costs by city, expected funding or scholarships, part‑time work assumptions, and budget caps), allowing per‑city/per‑option breakdowns within this single entry.

sections.label: Information Gaps and Research Tasks
sections.description: Capture all unanswered questions and all owned action items (research, outreach, document prep, campus visits, test booking) with clear owner and due date; do not record external portals’ deadlines here—those belong in External Deadlines and Milestones.

sections.label: Stakeholders and Decision Process
sections.description: Note who is involved in advising or deciding, who funds the studies, the intended decision cadence and checkpoints, and how tie‑breaks will be resolved.

sections.label: External Deadlines and Milestones
sections.description: Record externally set dates/windows and milestones such as application portal open/close periods, test dates/registration windows, Uni‑Assist/APS processing timelines, enrollment periods, and visa appointment lead times; do not list owned actions or assignees here.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.goal: Build rapport, clarify the student’s aims for studying in Germany, and agree on success criteria for this conversation.

phases.label: Map Options and Requirements
phases.goal: Elicit concrete programs/universities in scope, capture their admissions requirement types and current eligibility, establish initial budget constraints, and begin defining the global decision criteria.

phases.label: Compare and Narrow
phases.goal: Evaluate options against priorities and budget to form a prioritized shortlist and surface remaining unknowns.

phases.label: Plan and Wrap
phases.goal: Convert the shortlist into owned actions with due dates and align on external deadlines and decision checkpoints.

issues.description: No explicit place to capture the prioritized shortlist or per-option evaluation results. The phase evaluate_and_narrow aims to "form a prioritized shortlist," but neither candidate_universities_and_programs nor decision_criteria_and_priority_weights provides fields for ranking/status, fit scores, or pros/cons by criterion.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) add a new repeated section, e.g., shortlist_and_comparative_assessment, to record per-program ratings vs criteria, rank/status (longlist/shortlist/top choice), and rationale; or (b) expand candidate_universities_and_programs to include fields for priority/rank/status and brief per-criterion notes/scores.

issues.description: Linkage between admissions_requirements_and_eligibility and specific programs is implicit and could lead to mis-bucketing (aggregated notes instead of per-program requirements).
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify that each admissions_requirements_and_eligibility entry is per program and must reference a program in candidate_universities_and_programs (e.g., include a program_ref field or instruct "one entry per target program").

issues.description: The Map Options and Requirements phase front-loads both options discovery and budget setup; without a place for quick interim tagging of priorities, this phase may become bloated.
issues.suggested_fix: If not adding a separate comparative section, allow candidate_universities_and_programs to capture a lightweight preliminary priority tag (e.g., explore/viable/favorite) to keep flow efficient before the deeper evaluation phase.

critique.rationale: Overall the template is well-structured, Germany-specific, and aligns with the meeting’s goals of mapping options and decision factors. However, it lacks an explicit container to record the prioritized shortlist or per-program evaluations, which the later phase expects. Minor clarifications around tying admissions requirements to specific programs would prevent mis-bucketing during capture.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Add an explicit mechanism (new section or expanded fields) to capture per-option evaluation and a prioritized shortlist.
